class.name: VoxelTerrainNavigation
class.brief_description: Keeps a navigation mesh in step with a [VoxelTerrain] as it is edited.
class.description: Add as a child of a [VoxelTerrain]. The navmesh is split into square tiles, columns of [member tile_size_blocks] mesh blocks, each its own navigation region. When the voxels in a tile change (edited, or streamed in or out), the tile is rebaked on a worker thread once it has been quiet for [member bake_delay], or at least every [member max_bake_interval] while it keeps changing, and swapped in on the main thread. Only the tiles an edit can affect are rebaked: those whose baking area (the tile plus a border of about the agent's radius) the edited voxels reach. Each tile bakes the terrain's own triangles together with [member static_geometry], fixed scene geometry baked offline (buildings, roads, props' obstructions). Walkable parts of that geometry that voxels now bury are dropped (see [member drop_buried_static_geometry]), so filling a road in takes it off the navmesh and digging it out puts it back. Things that move but stand in the way carve the navmesh too: [NavigationObstacle3D] nodes in [member obstacle_group] with [member NavigationObstacle3D.affect_navigation_mesh] enabled. An obstacle's footprint is its vertices, or a circle of its radius, around its global position; its prism reaches from the agent's height below it to its height above, so ground a walker would hit it from counts as blocked. When one moves more than a quarter metre, appears or goes away, the tiles it leaves and enters are rebaked. Settings (agent size, slope, climb, cell size) come from [member template_navigation_mesh]. Its cell size has to divide a tile into a whole number of cells, or neighbouring tiles will not join up; with [member configure_map] the navigation map's cell size and height are set to match.

method.name: bake_all
method.description: Marks every tile for rebaking now, without waiting for [member bake_delay].

method.name: get_pending_tile_count
method.description: Tiles waiting to bake or baking. Zero once the navmesh matches the terrain.

method.name: get_statistics
method.description: Tile and bake counts and timings: [code]tiles[/code], [code]pending_tiles[/code], [code]bakes_in_flight[/code], [code]bake_count[/code], [code]bake_usec_last[/code], [code]bake_usec_max[/code], [code]bake_usec_average[/code] (worker time), [code]apply_usec_max[/code] (main thread), [code]dropped_results[/code] (bakes outdated before they finished), [code]edit_changes[/code] and [code]block_changes[/code] (mesh changes reported as edited boxes, or as whole blocks).

members.member: Seconds a tile has to go without changes before it is rebaked, so an edit made in steps bakes once.
If true, sets the navigation map's cell size and height to the template's.

If true, walkable triangles of [member static_geometry] with solid voxels half the agent's height above them are left out of the bake. A baker sees only surfaces, not what is solid between them, so a road under a deep fill would otherwise still read as a walkable floor with the fill's top for a ceiling.
While false, nothing is baked and the tiles' regions are disabled. Turn it on only where agents path, a multiplayer host for example.
A tile that keeps changing (someone digging in it) is still rebaked at least this often.
Tile bakes allowed to run at once, as low-priority tasks on [WorkerThreadPool], which leaves the voxel engine's own threads free for meshing.
Navigation layers of the tiles' regions.

Group whose [NavigationObstacle3D] members (with affect_navigation_mesh) carve the navmesh where they stand. With [member NavigationObstacle3D.carve_navigation_mesh] off, the agent's radius is kept clear round them too.
If true, also bakes while the scene is open in the editor.

Fixed geometry baked into every tile it overlaps, in world space: typically parsed once from the level's static colliders with [method NavigationServer3D.parse_source_geometry_data] and saved, with projected obstructions for props a bake can't see.
Settings every tile bakes with. Its own polygons are not used.
Width of a tile, in mesh blocks. Smaller tiles rebake less per edit; larger ones mean fewer regions.
